headline: NO SANDWICHES
chyron: SANDWICH SHOP RUNS OUT OF SANDWICHES
ticker: SANDWICH SHOP "OUT OF SANDWICHES, NOT OF SPIRIT"
BAKERY ALSO OUT OF BREAD, "ADMITTEDLY A WORRY"
CAREERCRASH.ORG: THE CHEF WAS ASKED. DECLINED TO COMMENT. THREW A PAN

beats.text: Breaking tonight: a sandwich shop has run out of sandwiches. Our foreign correspondent Rupert Fennimore-Twistleton is there.
Philippa. I am standing outside a sandwich shop which, as of eleven o'clock this morning, has no sandwiches.
I asked the owner for a cheese and pickle. No. A BLT? No. Egg mayonnaise? Not as such.
Rupert, Brock here. Did you try the tuna?
No, Brock. Not the tuna. Not even the tuna.
Coronation chicken? Ploughman's? The so-called Club? Nothing. The shop is, I'm afraid, completely uncontaminated by sandwiches.
Then why is it still open?
Philippa, a shop is a state of mind.
A shop is not a state of mind, Brock. I checked. It's a state of planning permission.
Breaking: the owner has found a single crust. Crowds are gathering. It may be the last crust in
I'M GOING DOWN THERE. THAT CRUST IS MINE!

shouts.uk: IT'S NOT A STATE OF MIND!

realStory.text: Made up. It borrows from Monty Python's Cheese Shop sketch (1972), in which a cheese shop turns out to stock no cheese at all. Rupert has since been asked to stop calling sandwich shops "the front".

signoff: Rupert bought the last crust and shared it with the owner. Half each.
